200	Extremely grave. And people, a baal teshuvah, who calls himself a rabbi... Woe
201	to us, "Rav et rivenu ve'edan et dinenu."
202	Therefore, a person who has holiness and closeness to HaShem must guard it
203	more than anything!
204	You have a dear friend, a merciful Father who loves you.
205	You have a relationship with Him of love, of devotion, of closeness, of speech.
206	Is that the most important thing to you in the world?
207	Don't sell it for a pot of lentil stew.
208	Don't sell it for a pot of lentil stew.
209	And every millimeter forward that you can come closer in a relationship with Him, even if it costs you blood,
210	tears and fasts, with your heart and your blood, pour it out, pour it out, and draw close to Him.
211	The main thing is to be more His friend, closer to Him.
212	Isn't it told of Rabbi Eliyahu Mani, peace be upon him, that they called him a chasid? And why was he a chasid? Because every
213	extra piety he could take, he took upon himself. Once Rabbi Efraim Cohen told, and why did he take on pieties?
214	To cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He, to come a little closer to Him, one more millimeter. Once he was studying
215	Etz Chaim and didn't understand. He reviewed it and didn't understand. He opened the window, not knowing
216	that the room was empty. His yeshiva was in Hebron.
217	He was the rabbi of Hebron, and one of the rabbis was there, the door was
218	open, and he saw the rabbi open the window and say: Master of the Universe, I don't understand. How many
219	fasts have I already fasted, how many mortifications have I already undergone, what more do You want me to take upon myself
220	that I haven't taken? See what this is, how far he got: what more do You
221	want me to take upon myself that I haven't taken?
222	I have already taken on every extra piety I can, I have stretched myself to the limit of my ability.
223	So a person who is a servant of HaShem, who draws close to the Holy One, blessed be He, as much as he can, is stringent upon himself.
224	Not everything is lenient. "Everything, they were accustomed to be lenient" — those are laws for after the fact.
225	There are those who are experts in the laws of after the fact.
226	After the fact it's possible, but after the fact it's permitted.
227	Haven't I told you a thousand times that someone calls me?
228	He asks me a question, whether it's permitted or forbidden. I told him, "Forbidden." He says to me, "Rabbi,
229	think again. Tell me, are you serious?" I tell you,
230	"Forbidden." He says to me, "Maybe nevertheless you'll find some way to permit it?" I told him,
231	"The Gemara, the Yerushalmi, the Shulchan Aruch and the Rambam all ruled to forbid." He says to me, "Ya Allah, you
232	are already the eighth rabbi who tells me it's forbidden. Have mercy, what are you looking for?
233	A goat in your place to go to Azazel?
234	To go to Gehinnom in your place?
235	What is it with you? Forbidden is forbidden." There are those who are experts in the laws of after the fact.
236	"Listen, but after the fact it's permitted, but after the fact there's a custom to be lenient, but after the fact, but after the fact."
237	Instead of being one who keeps away from a hundred gates of after the fact, for a hundred
238	gates of permissibility, in order not to stumble in a single after the fact.
239	A person who is a servant of HaShem: "On my bed at night I sought the one my soul loves," seeking still more closeness to HaShem,
